newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish labour reform up to government - Pujol.
newsitem.headline: Spanish labour reform up to government - Pujol.

text.p: Catalan leader Jordi Pujol said on Friday responsibility for a labour reform deal lies with the government and not employers and unions.

"It would be great if employers and unions could reach a deal without the government adding a comma, but the responsibility lies with parliament and the government," he said in an opening speech at a conference in northern Spain.
After three days of intensive talks, employers and unions said late on Thursday they would take a temporary break in negotiations to consider new proposals and would resume talks next Wednesday.
Without wanting to "rush" the two sides, Pujol pointed out that the informal deadline imposed for a deal had expired on Tuesday.
The government has given the two sides until early March to reach a deal before it steps in and imposes a package of measures.
However, the government said on Thursday it would be patient for an accord.
"A good agreement is better than a quick agreement," Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez-Cascos said.
Employers have been fighting for more flexibility in the job market and an easing of redundancy regulations while unions are calling for more security, especially for youths.
The current deadlock lies in contracts for youths.
Former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez said on Friday he supported the introduction of more flexibility into the labour market, but warned this must not come at the expense of more insecurity.
"The labour reforms must be directed at creating flexibility, but flexibility must come with added security for citizens," he told the conference.
He said he hoped that an agreement would be reached next Wednesday.
